templateVariables.title: Available variables

context.item: Central reference for item templates and linked source data.
context.source: Central reference for source templates, dependencies, and loops.

templateVariables.sid: Accesses linked source data by source id. The key starts with s followed by the source id.
templateVariables.sn: Accesses linked source data by source name. Use bracket notation when the name contains spaces or special characters.
templateVariables.get: Contains GET parameters from the current URL. Each key returns a list of values.
templateVariables.var: Accesses global computed variables configured in the visual template.
templateVariables.var_loop: Accesses computed variables inside the current visual template loop.
templateVariables.secret: Accesses an encrypted secret in a source template. The secret filter decrypts the value on the backend.
templateVariables.source_item: Only available in a source with a loop. Represents the current element from the iterated collection.
templateVariables.value: In an item template loop, contains the current value.
templateVariables.key: In an item template loop, contains the index or key for the current value.
templateVariables.object_item: In an item template loop, contains the current object. This is not the same item variable as source loops.
templateVariables.note: Paths after these variables follow the actual data structure returned by the sources.

getVariables.source_help: Values saved with the source and used by default in previews and editors.
getVariables.object_variable_help: Local override for this item variable. By default, the source value is used.

global.docsbytype: Each section contains its own dedicated documentation

bootstrap.description: Use Bootstrap classes in your HTML code to unify and customize the visual rendering of your items. The documentation contains many examples for each desired rendering.

icons.description: Use Font Awesome or Bootstrap icons to display items. The documentation contains many examples for each desired rendering.

datatable.description: DataTables allows you to easily add search, sorting, export, and pagination to your HTML tables. To use the Bootstrap theme, add the 'table' class. Refer to the documentation for examples and more information.

mermaid.description: Mermaid allows you to create diagrams. Must be contained in a 'pre' tag with the class 'mermaid'. Refer to the documentation for more information.

vueflow.description: Vue Flow allows you to create interactive diagrams made of nodes and links. Must be contained in a 'div' tag with the 'data-vueflow' attribute, holding the nodes and the edges in JSON. Refer to the documentation for more information.
vueflow.dump: The configuration can also be built from your source data. The 'safe' filter is not needed.
vueflow.sizing_description: A diagram has no height of its own and needs one to be displayed. Pick the mode that suits your view.
vueflow.sizing_aspect: Height computed from the width, keeping the given proportions. Recommended: it adapts to every screen size and to both kinds of view.
vueflow.sizing_fixed: Fixed height, in pixels. Use it when the diagram must always keep the same size, or when 'Adjusted sizing' is enabled on the object.
vueflow.sizing_fill: Fills the height left in the object. In a grid view the diagram takes the height of its slot, in a row view the height of the tallest object of the line. Cannot be combined with 'Adjusted sizing'.
vueflow.options_description: Every option of the Vue Flow documentation is available: on each node, on each edge, and on the diagram itself (fitViewOnInit, snapToGrid, minZoom, connectionMode, background, controls, minimap, and so on).
vueflow.events_description: The diagram emits an event on every interaction, which the JavaScript code of the object can listen to.

nunjucks.description: Nunjucks allows you to define templates. Use the data from your sources to build your structure on these data (loops, conditions, ...). Refer to the documentation for more information.

date.description: Allows to manipulate the format of dates.

find.description: Allows to search for a value in an array of objects and return the first object that matches.

fromjson.description: Allows to convert a JSON string to an object.

setattribute.description: Allows to modify an attribute of an object.

split.description: Allows splitting a string into an array using a separator.

javascript.description: The JavaScript code is executed after the HTML code and can use Nunjucks. It is important to note that each datalchemist object can contain its own associated JavaScript code, so it is recommended to avoid potential conflicts with other objects by using unique variable or function names and minimizing the impact on the global environment.
